terms.plain_language: The Political MAYHEM translation for the Australian public/electorate as the foundational non-parliamentary body that directly selects representatives and participates in constitutional referendums.
terms.research_use: Keep the public structurally prior to parliamentary teams without inventing a party, roster or continuous synthetic score.

terms.plain_language: An alternate interface description for the First Team emphasising that it exists outside the parliamentary competition and is not another party team.
terms.research_use: Prevent the public from being displayed as a parliamentary competitor while preserving its constitutional-democratic role.

terms.plain_language: The separate evidence-backed form view for the First Team. It updates only from verifiable public decision points or measurable public-driven institutional outcomes and is not part of the party primary-vote ladder.
terms.research_use: Prevent polling, silence or political rhetoric from being substituted for an actual public result.

terms.plain_language: An election or referendum in which electors directly determine a constitutionally or electorally recognised outcome.
terms.research_use: Identify moments when First Team form can be grounded in an authoritative result rather than inferred sentiment.

terms.term: Team claim about the First Team
terms.plain_language: A claim by a party, government, parliamentarian or campaign that it speaks for Australians, ordinary people, the public interest or the will of the people.
terms.research_use: Classify the statement as positioning until the claimed public preference is independently evidenced for the relevant question and population.
